pr_title: [Transform] respect timeout parameters in all API's
pr_body:
make timeout parameter explicit in all transform actions and pass timeout values in sub-calls.

fixes #79268
pr_comments:
Pinging @elastic/es-core-infra

Please have a look at the proposed change to `AcknowledgedRequest`.

issue_context.title: [Transform] transform start call does not respect timeout parameter
issue_context.body:
**Affected version:** 7.13-7.15

In special cases starting a transform can take a long time, e.g. if CCS is involved and index patterns that resolve to a large number of indices. `_start` can take a `timeout` parameter (default `30s`):

```
POST /_transform/my_transform/_start?timeout=100s
```

However the `100s` are not respected in inner calls like validation. Instead of passing on the outer timeout or a share of it, no timeout is set, which means the default(`30s`) is used.

**Mitigation**

There is unfortunately no workaround. Its possible to reduce the complexity of the transform, e.g. using a query, in order to stay within the default timeout.

**Proposed fix**

Pass the timeout parameter from `_start` to inner validation calls.
comments: Update: it has been observed that this happens also at the “INSERT” stage. So even inserting exhibits the timeout after 5 minutes. I'm assuming it's the same issue due to identical symptoms but I don't have direct evidence.

> Update: it has been observed that this happens also at the “INSERT” stage. So even inserting exhibits the timeout after 5 minutes. I'm assuming it's the same issue due to identical symptoms but I don't have direct evidence.

Yes, correct. For `PUT` the timeout isn't passed to the underlying validation call either.

review_comments:
This is still a discrepancy with every other request class in the Elasticsearch codebase - all the others consider requests to be equal if they have different timeouts but the same arguments related to the actual action.  For example, the [create index request docs](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/indices-create-index.html#indices-create-api-query-params) show both `timeout` and `master_timeout` are supported.  But the create index request code checks neither when considering equality: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/68ee6d4fe102334168865c64d39a08c6e239f50f/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/admin/indices/create/CreateIndexRequest.java#L481-L493

I've searched for another request class that considers timeout part of equality and cannot find one.

You are assuming that's a bug across the whole Elasticsearch codebase and by changing it in transforms you're making a start on fixing it.  It may well be, as the pattern for checking request equality dates back to when there was only one person working on the codebase and it may have been a simple mistake that's been propagated repeatedly over the years.  But what if it's the intention that timeouts are not considered part of equality for requests?  Then you've introduced a bug into transforms.  It's a shame there are no comments to indicate.

> I've searched for another request class that considers timeout part of equality and cannot find one.

Actually I searched a bit harder and found three.  `ClusterRerouteRequest`: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a92a647b9f17d1bddf5c707490a19482c273eda3/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/admin/cluster/reroute/ClusterRerouteRequest.java#L140
`UpdateSettingsRequest`: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/f6801d2aea5457d6422d7e5c015f6b57b904b5af/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/admin/indices/settings/put/UpdateSettingsRequest.java#L242
and `DeleteDataFrameAnalyticsAction.Request`: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/20c9f756d28d116f0667e19a1b531aa80c55bde7/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/core/ml/action/DeleteDataFrameAnalyticsAction.java#L89

But that's three out of several hundred, so it still deserves wider discussion.

`CreateIndex` is an interesting one, if you go back in history:
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/commit/b3337c312765e51cec7bde5883bbc0a08f56fb65#diff-f919ea00a6a4a7c7c33395ac0a46d492e09a57a8fb827db92e184aa5c62d2513
you see that it originally had `timeout` but `equals` and `hashCode` has not been implemented. I think it has not been important back than.

I therefore think it has not been intentionally left out, but has been forgotten or as said, wasn't important.

It seems to me that `equals` and `hashCode` are only indirectly important for the product. It helps us in writing better unit tests and avoids silly - but hard to debug - issues in serialization and other areas.  That's why this PR adds a lot of test code that follows up on https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/25910 by implementing `mutateInstance` where it makes sense.
OK cool.  I'll assume it's best practice to consider timeouts in equality then, and the transform requests are now making a start on that.
